load_basis: Gross utility power capacity contracted with TVA at 'Paducah-Calvert City, Kentucky' in the Electric Utility Providers table of Core Scientific's FY2025 10-K (as of 2025-12-31); operator site page also lists 150 MW total power capacity. This is contracted/built capacity, not metered load.
notes: Address 1035 Shar-Cal Rd, Calvert City, KY 42029 (operator page), on a redeveloped former steel mill; coordinates from the U.S. Census geocoder for that address. TVA is named as the electric utility provider in the 10-K (high confidence on TVA); the direct-serve (wholesale_direct) arrangement is inferred from TVA itself being listed rather than a local power company, hence overall 'medium'. The Nov 2019 opening announcement reported 30+ MW deployed and 125 MW 'ready-now'. Bitcoin mining/hosting site; the 10-K says Core intends to convert its portfolio to high-density colocation, but no Kentucky conversion date was found. Not in known_facilities.

site_name: Riot Platforms Kentucky Facility - Commerce Drive (Block Mining, Paducah)
serving_utility: Jackson Purchase Energy Corporation (Big Rivers Electric Corporation wholesale, MISO)
load_basis: COMBINED figure for Riot's two Kentucky sites (Commerce Drive + Blue Steel); no per-site split is published. Riot FY2025 10-K Item 1: Kentucky Facility 'currently has approximately 137 MW of developed capacity' (filed 2026-03-02). The same 10-K's MD&A metrics table shows 192 MW developed power capacity at 2025-12-31 (60 MW at 2024-12-31) and 6.4 EH/s deployed; the two 10-K figures were not reconciled, and the lower one is used here.
notes: Address 5657 Commerce Drive, Paducah, KY 42001 (Block Mining's principal office and service address in the Jan 2026 JPEC/Big Rivers/Block Mining agreement filed with the KY PSC); coordinates are an OpenStreetMap Nominatim geocode of that address. Riot's site page says Commerce 'energized and started operations in February 2022'. Jackson Purchase Energy is the retail seller under Big Rivers wholesale (WKMS May 2026: Riot signed two PPAs with JPEC through 2043). This appears to be the same Industrial Park West facility approved as 'Blockware Mining' in PSC Case 2021-00282 (same park, same utility pair, same Feb 2022 energization; 30 MW at its Aug 2022 opening) - that identity is an inference, not a documented name change. To avoid double counting, the Blue Steel row carries null load. At the July 2024 acquisition the two sites totaled 60 MW. planned_full_buildout_mw = Riot's 232 MW target for the combined Kentucky Facility through 2026; separate 2026 PSC filings cover a new Commerce Park site and a 'Shell Site' at 14110 Ogden Landing Rd, Kevil (neither operating in 2025). Riot's web page states a 'combined operational capacity of 300 MW', which conflicts with the 10-K and was not used. Not in known_facilities.

site_name: Riot Platforms Kentucky Facility - Blue Steel (Block Mining, Calvert City)
serving_utility: Tennessee Valley Authority (local power company vs. direct service not identified)
notes: Load is included in the combined 137 MW on the Commerce Drive row (Riot reports its two Kentucky sites together); left null here to avoid double counting. Kentucky Lantern's tracker (updated Aug 2026) describes a 25 MW Riot site near Calvert City operating since the 2024 acquisition. Riot's site page says Blue Steel 'energized and started operations in March 2024'. Utility is an inference by elimination: 2024 acquisition coverage says Block Mining's sites are served by TVA and Big Rivers, and the Paducah site is documented as Jackson Purchase/Big Rivers, so the Calvert City site is presumably the TVA-served one; no primary document found. Riot's 10-K separately says MISO oversees its Kentucky power supply, which fits the Paducah site only. No published street address found, so no coordinates. Not in known_facilities.

serving_utility: West Kentucky Rural Electric Cooperative Corporation (TVA power)
load_basis: Soluna FY2025 10-K: 'Project Sophie is a 25 MW data center, based in Murray, Kentucky connected to the grid'; listed as Operating; operator project page shows 25 MW energized. Nameplate site capacity, subject to contractual curtailment.
notes: Bitcoin hosting site on a 3.2-acre tract in Murray bought March 2021 (10-K Item 2); 10-K says the facility 'was completed in 2021' (year is completion, exact energization month not stated). FY2022 10-K says the site 'is powered by the TVA grid' and names Western Kentucky Rural Electric Cooperative (WKRECC) in connection with managing excess energy; the retail seller is therefore read as WKRECC, a TVA local power company, but no document states that outright. FY2025 10-K says the PPA requires curtailment during certain hours, hence special_contract. No street address appears in SEC filings; a directory-only address lead was not used, so coordinates are null. Soluna's other Kentucky site, Project Marie (20 MW, Calvert City, TVA), was shut down in early 2023 and is excluded. Not in known_facilities.

load_basis: KY PSC final order, Case 2022-00371 (2023-08-07): estimated load 2 MW as of 2022-09-28 rising to 13 MW by May 2023 at a 95 percent load factor; contract covers load of up to 13 MW. Contract estimate, not a 2025 measurement; 2023 press described a constant 10 MW.
notes: Cryptocurrency mine at a former coal mining site in Waverly, Union County, served by KU under an Economic Development Rider special contract approved by the PSC on 2023-08-07 (ten-year term). No street address in the order, so coordinates are null. Operating status in 2025 was not independently confirmed. Not in known_facilities.

site_name: North Campbell Land Co. (Sphere 3D) Hopkinsville mine at HES Holland Substation
load_basis: Hoptown Chronicle (July 2026): existing bitcoin operation of 15 MW, 22 modular units, inside Hopkinsville Electric System's Holland Substation.
notes: Located inside HES's Holland Substation on North Campbell Street (no street number published; coordinates null). Start year is approximate: the July 2026 article says the mine had run for about three years. Owner proposes converting the 15 MW to other computing and building a separate 50 MW data center elsewhere in Hopkinsville with a new 65 MW HES substation (not operating in 2025, so not included in buildout here). Contract type with HES not stated. Not in known_facilities.
